results.fact: Which approach and camp are used to reach Massie Peak's West Ridge
results.evidence: The Chiwawa River Trail / 'M' tree / ford / sheepherder path to Massie Lake is documented (about 4 mi up the Chiwawa, then an unmaintained path to the lake; the lake spur is given as 1.9 mi and 1,500 ft). But Massie Peak is also climbed from a Buck Creek Pass basecamp on multi-peak loops (an Aug-2024 report covers Buck Creek Pass, High Pass, Cleator, Helmet Butte, Massie, Liberty Cap), so the itinerary's approach is a real alternative rather than invented. The itinerary is nonetheless garbled (it routes 'past High Pass', which lies beyond Buck Creek Pass away from Massie, to a 'south basin' camp and then onto the Massie Lake High Route), and no two sources give the miles/gain/hours needed to rewrite a Chiwawa/Massie Lake itinerary, so no patch is written. The whole itinerary (3 days, 29 mi), timing.sectionBreakdown and partner_requirements.fitnessSpec need a rewrite once one approach is chosen.

The row puts Massie Lake at ~6,600-6,700 ft (approach, and ~6,600 ft 'south basin' in itinerary), 4,800 ft (waypoint), and 'roughly 1,500 ft above the turnoff' (bivy). The lake spur is described as 1.5-1.9k ft of gain from the Chiwawa (~3,300 ft), implying ~4,800-5,200 ft, while the USGS elevation service at the GNIS point for Massie Lake (48.1332, -120.9014) returns ~5,936 ft. The sources do not agree, so no patch.

results.correct_value: Snow Lakes Trailhead -> Nada/Snow Lakes -> Lake Viviane -> leave trail at ~7,000 ft between Leprechaun and Sprite Lakes -> SSE to the notch west of the Prong -> south side of the ridge to the summit block
results.evidence: The standard route leaves the trail at the flat ~7,000 ft area between Leprechaun and Sprite Lakes, climbs SSE keeping west of the Prong to McClellan Ridge, then goes east on the south side of the ridge, the southeast side of the block being easiest. A Snow Lakes party went Snow Lake -> Lake Viviane -> past Leprechaun Lake -> Prong notch -> class 3-4 to the summit. The Ingalls Creek/Crystal Creek text (face, pitch_detail, obj_haz '~18 miles', 'gully above 6,000 ft', 'Fantasia Saddle/Pond') is a separate, real southern route (Ingalls Creek TH, ~18 mi RT, 6,300+ ft); the Colchuck/Aasgard beta is another real approach but contradicts every other field on this row. These fields were rewritten to the Snow Lakes line that the approach, waypoints, itinerary, timing, descent and approach_variants all describe.

results.fact: End of the reliable snow/ice season on the face
results.correct_value: early June to mid-July; July still good early/mid-month
results.evidence: best_season, climate.summer and season ('Jun-Jul (best)') put the reliable window through about mid-July. A party climbed the face on 23 July 2022 with continuous snow and a firm upper section, and other July reports describe snow nearly to the summit. A June 2005 ascent found soft snow and cornice fall, so June is not uniquely reliable. seasonal_guidance (and the itinerary cal / climate.bySeason 'early July') were aligned to June-mid-July.
